gen.title: Balanced forces in steady level flight

cards.stem: In steady level flight with constant speed, how do vertical forces compare?
options: lift is equal to the weight
lift is greater than the weight
drag is equal to the weight
thrust is greater than the weight
cards.quote: an airplane can maintain a constant speed and level flight, in which the lift is equal to the weight, and the thrust is equal to the drag.
cards.hint: Consider vertical equilibrium in level flight

cards.stem: In steady level flight with constant speed, how do horizontal forces compare?
options: thrust is equal to the drag
thrust is greater than the drag
lift is equal to the drag
weight is equal to the thrust
cards.quote: the thrust is equal to the drag.
cards.hint: Think about horizontal equilibrium for steady speed

cards.stem: What external condition lets an aircraft keep its airspeed without accelerating?
options: no net external force
no net internal force
net external force at maximum
airspeed keeps increasing
cards.quote: Since there is no net external force on the aircraft, the aircraft maintains a constant airspeed as described by Newton’s First Law of Motion.
cards.hint: Recall the law describing motion with zero net force

cards.stem: When forces no longer balance in flight, what does the aircraft do?
options: moves in the direction of the greater force
moves opposite the greater force
remains at constant airspeed
maintains level flight
cards.quote: if the forces become unbalanced, the aircraft moves in the direction of the greater force.
cards.hint: Unbalanced force dictates new motion direction
